name: Bach Ma: Five Lakes and the summit (Hải Vọng Đài)
region: Bach Ma National Park, between Hue and Da Nang
why: Two short walks at the top of a former French hill station: a stair path down to a chain of pools in the cloud forest, then up to a tower with the coast and the lagoons below.
book: Pay the entrance fee at the park gate near Cau Hai, about 40 km south of Hue. Motorbikes and bicycles are not allowed on the steep 16 km summit road: book the park car or come with a car and driver. Ask at the gate whether the road is open to the top.
water: Carry 1.5 litres; the pools are for swimming, not drinking. Drinks only at the park guesthouses near the summit.
dangers: One of the wettest places in Vietnam: rain and fog most of the year, heavy rain and typhoons from September to December.
Slippery stone steps and rocks at the Five Lakes, and leeches after rain.
Cool at 1,400 m even in summer: carry a rain jacket and a warm layer.
turnaround: In heavy rain skip the Five Lakes steps (the stream rises fast) and walk only to the summit tower.

points.name: Five Lakes trailhead, km 17 of the summit road
points.note: By the checkpoint on the summit road. The Five Lakes path goes down from here; the summit path climbs from the same bend.

points.name: Five Lakes (Ngũ Hồ)
points.note: Stone steps lead down to five pools linked by small falls on a granite stream. Come back up the same steps.

points.name: Bach Ma summit tower (Hải Vọng Đài)
points.note: About 1,450 m. From the tower: the Annamite ridges, Cau Hai lagoon and the sea when the cloud lifts. Walk back down to the road.
